query: Starting from crystalline, near-equiatomic solid-solution nanoparticles composed of five or more metals, what single intervention could overcome the unresolved risk of structural or chemical instability during operation in the 773–1173 K catalytic regime? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, the mechanism by which it would preserve stability, the predicted outcome relative to the same nanoparticles without the intervention, relevant temperature, time, and compositional boundary conditions, supporting prior evidence, and a thermal-exposure experiment with measurements and failure criteria that could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introduction of a gradient in composition from the surface to the core of the nanoparticles
generation.material_initial_state: Crystalline, near-equiatomic solid-solution nanoparticles composed of five or more metals
generation.intervention: Gradient in composition from surface to core
generation.mechanism: Reduced lattice strain and improved resistance to chemical segregation
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved structural and chemical stability during operation
generation.boundary: Temperature: 773–1173 K, Time: dependent on operation conditions, Composition: near-equiatomic solid-solution of five or more metals
generation.uncertainty: Lack of specific data on the effects of compositional gradients on stability in multi-metallic nanoparticles

falsification_experiment.design: Thermal-exposure experiment with nanoparticles with and without compositional gradient
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If nanoparticles with compositional gradient show no improvement in structural and chemical stability compared to those without, the hypothesis is falsified
